To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel aptamer/antibodies sandwich assay provides highly specific and sensitive detection of proteins on the surface of ProteinChip arrays.
a rapid method for screening specific nucleic acid-protein interaction on ProteinChip arrays has been developed.

a new method for the rapid screening of proteins bound to thioaptamer probes anchored to ProteinChip array surfaces was developed, and the specific binding proteins identified by tandem MS and confirmed by thioaptamer sandwich assay were heterogeneous nuclear ribonuclear proteins (hnRNPs).
In summary, our research is concerned with
a rapid, sensitive, and specific method to screen and to identify unknown bound proteins from complex biological samples to specific nucleic acids anchored on ProteinChip surfaces.
the identification of specific proteins bound to a specific aptamer probe on a ProteinChip array.

a novel approach for rapid identification of proteins from crude biological samples by direct coupling of nucleic acid probes to ProteinChip array surfaces, which is a powerful tool for screening and identification of proteins that bind to specific nucleic acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thioaptamer-based method provides a novel approach to rapidly screen and identify specific binding proteins to nucleic acid probes from crude biological samples.
the thioaptamer-based proteomic array technology is a promising and powerful tool in screening specific protein targets from crude biological samples.
a rapid and efficient screening and identification of unknown "on-chip"-bound proteins to nucleic acid probes on ProteinChip arrays has been achieved by this new method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a rapid, sensitive, and specific method has been developed in our laboratory to screen and identify specific proteins bound to specific nucleic acids anchored on ProteinChip surfaces from crude biological extracts, which may be used for the identification of specific nucleic acid binding proteins from a variety of biological samples.
the thioaptamer probes can be used to capture specific proteins from crude biological extracts and that the captured proteins can be identified by microsequencing.
the combination of aptamers and ProteinChip technology has been demonstrated for the first time as a novel and powerful tool for proteomics studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thioaptamer-based ProteinChip array system is a powerful tool for screening and identifying specific proteins in crude biological samples.
a rapid method for identification of proteins bound to specific nucleic acids anchored on ProteinChip arrays from complex samples has been developed.
this new approach can be applied to the identification of specific binding proteins in crude biological samples.
